chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about the qamis (shirt) whose warp is silk and its weft is from yarn. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if one enters into Ihram wearing it; rather, what is disliked is the pure (silk) from it.'

key_terms.الْخَمِيصَة: A type of shirt or tunic, commonly worn by men in Ihram.
key_terms.الْغَزْل: Yarn or thread, typically referring to wool, cotton, or linen in this context.
key_terms.يُحْرَمَ: Enters into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration).

ai.seo_question: Can a man wear a silk-mixed shirt while in the state of Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between pure silk (khāṣṣ) and mixed silk (muḍāf) regarding the validity of Ihram, establishing that the prohibition is specific to the latter's exclusivity. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the restriction on silk for men in Ihram is based on the principle of avoiding luxury items reserved for women or the wealthy, rather than a blanket ban on all silk blends. This ruling facilitates practical ease for pilgrims while maintaining the spiritual integrity of the state of consecration.
